strengths: Annual revenue rose to 65,179 million in 2025 from 45,043 million in 2024 (revenue growth_yoy = 0.447; 44.7%), driven by higher volumes and favorable mix (notably Mounjaro and Zepbound).
Net income rose to 20,640 million in 2025, with net margin of 31.67% and ROE of 77.78%, indicating strong profitability and efficient capital use.
ROE of 77.78% and current ratio of 1.5791 support a healthy balance sheet leverage and liquidity position given growth investments.

Debt-to-equity of 1.5402 shows the company finances expansion but remains within a manageable levered profile alongside strong cash generation (operating cash flow of 16.8B in 2025; 27.4B YTD through 9M 2026 per latest quarterly data).

Major products Mounjaro and Zepbound contributed a large portion of revenue (6+ major products collectively accounted for 82% of 2025 revenue; Mounjaro and Zepbound alone ~56%), highlighting strong growth engines.
risks: Revenue concentration risk: 82% of 2025 revenue comes from a relatively small set of products (notably Mounjaro and Zepbound), leaving results sensitive to competition, regulatory actions, or market shifts for these products.

Regulatory and pricing risk: U.S. price controls and payer regulations (IRA, Medicare/Medicaid pricing actions) are ongoing and could compress long-term revenue; recent government price-setting initiatives for obesity/incretin medicines could accelerate pricing erosion.
340B and insulin pricing litigation and investigations: ongoing actions related to 340B, insulin pricing, and other pricing investigations could pose legal and financial exposure.
High leverage driven by acquisitions: total debt rose to 49.5B by 9/30/2026 (vs 42.5B at 12/31/2025), raising leverage risk if macro headwinds intensify or growth slows.
Acquisition integration risk: rapid acquisitions (e.g., Centessa, Kelonia, Ventyx, and others) increase integration complexity and potential for higher IPR&D charges and one-time costs.
Cybersecurity and global operations risk: reliance on complex global IT systems and third-party vendors introduces cybersecurity and supply chain risks.
Foreign currency and commodity/macro volatility: as a global company, FX and inflation risks can affect results, even with hedging.
fundamentals.summary: LLY demonstrates a healthy and expanding business with strong top-line growth (revenue up ~45% in 2025 vs 2024 and ~39–46% growth in the latest quarter/year-to-date), above-average profitability (net margin ~31.7%; ROE ~77.8%), and solid liquidity (current ratio ~1.58; debt-to-equity ~1.54). Operating cash flow surged to 16.8B in 2025 and continued robust cash generation in 9M 2026 supports ongoing investments and share repurchases. The core growth drivers are the incretin/diabetes portfolio (Mounjaro and Zepbound), which alone plus other major products accounted for about 82% of 2025 revenue, underscoring strong internal demand but also concentration risk. The filings highlight substantial regulatory and pricing headwinds (IRA, NRDL dynamics, 340B) and significant acquisition-related spending and debt, which could pose risks if growth decelerates. Overall, the fundamentals point to a healthy and improving business trajectory, though leverage from recent acquisitions and regulatory pricing pressures warrant careful monitoring.
